    "tierOrComponent": "Paper 1 Introductory topics in psychology (7182/1)",
    "formatSummary": "Written paper, 120 minutes, 96 marks total. Four compulsory sections of 24 marks each: Social influence, Memory, Attachment, Approaches in Psychology. Answer all questions in every section. No choice. Mix of short-answer (1–4 marks), applied scenario questions and extended 8/16-mark evaluation questions. AO1, AO2 and AO3 are assessed across all sections.",
    "confidence": "high"
  },
  "title": "AQA A-level Psychology Paper 1: Introductory topics in psychology (7182/1) — Practice Paper",
  "instructions": [
    "Answer all questions in Section A, Section B, Section C and Section D.",
    "The paper carries 96 marks in total and lasts 2 hours.",
    "Questions in Section A (Social influence), Section B (Memory), Section C (Attachment) and Section D (Approaches in Psychology) are each worth 24 marks.",
    "Where a question includes a scenario, apply your psychological knowledge to the material presented.",
    "For extended writing questions, marks are awarded for knowledge (AO1) and for analysis, interpretation and evaluation (AO3) as indicated in the question.",
    "Do all rough work in the space provided; cross through any work you do not want marked.",
    "Calculators are not required for this paper."
  ],
  "companionDocuments": [],
  "durationMinutes": 120,
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1",
      "label": "Question 1",
      "prompt": "Define what is meant by conformity.",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q2",
      "label": "Question 2",
      "prompt": "Outline the difference between compliance and internalisation as types of conformity.",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q3",
      "label": "Question 3",
      "prompt": "A student reads about a study in which participants were asked to judge the length of a line alongside confederates who deliberately gave the same wrong answer. On trials where the confederates disagreed with each other, participants' conformity dropped sharply.\n\nExplain what this finding suggests about the role of unanimity in conformity.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q4",
      "label": "Question 4",
      "prompt": "Discuss research into obedience. Refer to Milgram's baseline study and at least one situational variable that affects obedience in your answer.\n\n[16 marks]",
      "marks": 16,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q5",
      "label": "Question 5",
      "prompt": "A new employee at a warehouse is told by colleagues that everyone starts work at 07:30, even though the official start time is 08:00. The employee arrives at 07:30 the next day without questioning it.\n\nIdentify the type of social influence most likely to explain the employee's behaviour. Justify your answer.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q6",
      "label": "Question 6",
      "prompt": "Outline the authoritarian personality as an explanation of obedience.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q7",
      "label": "Question 7",
      "prompt": "A campaign team wants to reduce the number of drivers who use their phones while driving. They design a message showing a driver losing control of the car after glancing at a text.\n\nUsing your knowledge of minority influence and/or social change, explain how the campaign team could increase the effectiveness of their message.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q8",
      "label": "Question 8",
      "prompt": "Outline the multi-store model of memory. Refer to sensory register, short-term memory and long-term memory in your answer.",
      "marks": 6,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q9",
      "label": "Question 9",
      "prompt": "A researcher reads a list of 20 words aloud to participants. Half the participants are asked to count backwards in threes from 100 immediately after hearing the list. The other half sit quietly for the same amount of time. The researcher then asks all participants to recall as many words as they can.\n\nIdentify the independent variable in this study.",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q10",
      "label": "Question 10",
      "prompt": "Explain one limitation of the interference theory of forgetting.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q11",
      "label": "Question 11",
      "prompt": "A witness to a robbery later reads a news article describing the robber as 'tall and aggressive'. When interviewed by police, the witness recalls the robber as taller and more aggressive than they originally reported.\n\nOutline what this example suggests about memory, referring to the work of Loftus and Palmer in your answer.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q12",
      "label": "Question 12",
      "prompt": "Discuss the cognitive interview as a way of improving the accuracy of eyewitness testimony.\n\n[16 marks]",
      "marks": 16,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q13",
      "label": "Question 13",
      "prompt": "A nursery worker notices that a toddler becomes very distressed when their mother leaves the room, but is easily comforted when she returns and continues playing happily.\n\nIdentify the attachment type most likely to be shown by this toddler. Justify your answer.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q14",
      "label": "Question 14",
      "prompt": "Outline what is meant by reciprocity in caregiver–infant interactions.",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q15",
      "label": "Question 15",
      "prompt": "A psychologist claims that a child's first attachment relationship acts as a template for all later relationships.\n\nOutline the term used to describe this claim.",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q16",
      "label": "Question 16",
      "prompt": "Discuss research into the influence of early attachment on later relationships, including the role of the internal working model. Refer to evidence from both animal and human studies in your answer.\n\n[16 marks]",
      "marks": 16,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q17",
      "label": "Question 17",
      "prompt": "A researcher observes that infants raised in an institution with high staff turnover show delays in forming specific attachments.\n\nUsing your knowledge of research into institutionalisation, explain one way this finding could inform improvements in childcare practice.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q18",
      "label": "Question 18",
      "prompt": "Outline the learning theory of attachment, including classical and operant conditioning in your answer.",
      "marks": 6,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q19",
      "label": "Question 19",
      "prompt": "A student says, 'I only revise subjects I enjoy, so I do well in them, which makes me enjoy them more.'\n\nIdentify the approach in psychology most likely to explain this student's behaviour. Justify your answer.",
      "reciprocity": null,
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q20",
      "label": "Question 20",
      "prompt": "Outline what psychologists mean by inference. Give one example of how a cognitive psychologist might use inference.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q21",
      "label": "Question 21",
      "prompt": "A therapist helps a client identify irrational thoughts about failing exams and replace them with more realistic beliefs. The client's anxiety decreases over several sessions.\n\nIdentify the approach in psychology most likely to explain this therapy. Justify your answer.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q22",
      "label": "Question 22",
      "prompt": "Discuss the psychodynamic approach in psychology. In your answer, refer to the role of the unconscious and the structure of personality.\n\n[16 marks]",
      "marks": 16,
      "social_influence": null,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q23",
      "label": "Question 23",
      "prompt": "Outline one similarity and one difference between the humanistic approach and the psychodynamic approach.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q24",
      "label": "Question 24",
      "prompt": "A psychologist measures how quickly participants press a button when a light appears. The psychologist claims the reaction time data can be used to make inferences about internal mental processes such as attention.\n\nExplain why the cognitive approach relies on inference when studying mental processes.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q25",
      "label": "Question 25",
      "prompt": "Outline the role of defence mechanisms in the psychodynamic approach. Give one example of a defence mechanism.",
      "projection": null,
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q26",
      "label": "Question 26",
      "prompt": "A researcher wants to investigate whether the presence of a mobile phone affects students' ability to concentrate on a reading task. The researcher randomly allocates 40 students to two groups. Group A completes the reading task with a phone on the desk. Group B completes the same task with no phone present. Concentration is measured by the number of errors made on a comprehension test afterwards.\n\nIdentify the experimental design used in this study. Explain one advantage of this design.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "phone": null,
      "id": "q27",
      "label": "Question 27",
      "prompt": "A student claims, 'I revise with music playing because it helps me focus.' A psychologist suggests the student is making a type of explanation that ignores free will.\n\nUsing your knowledge of the free will/determinism debate, explain the psychologist's suggestion.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q28",
      "label": "Question 28",
      "prompt": "Outline the emergence of psychology as a science. Refer to Wundt's contribution in your answer.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "from": null,
      "id": "q29",
      "label": "Question 29",
      "prompt": "A psychologist uses a case study of one individual with a rare memory condition to draw conclusions about how memory works in the general population.\n\nOutline one limitation of using a case study to make generalisations about memory.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q30",
      "label": "Question 30",
      "by": null,
      "prompt": "Discuss the humanistic approach in psychology. In your answer, refer to self-actualisation and the role of the self.\n\n[16 marks]",
      "marks": 16,
      "assets": []
    }
  ],
  "choiceGroups": [],

  "examinerInsights": [
    "In 16-mark discussion questions, candidates often describe studies in detail but lose AO3 credit by not explicitly evaluating methodology, such as sampling, validity or ethical issues.",
    "Applied scenario questions reward precise use of psychological terminology rather than general description; candidates should name the concept before applying it.",
    "For Social influence, candidates frequently conflate the three types of conformity; clear definitions with an example earn full AO1 credit.",
    "In Memory, candidates often describe the multi-store model without linking research evidence to specific stores; explicit links earn higher marks.",
    "In Attachment, the strange situation categories are frequently confused; candidates should learn the behavioural characteristics of each type precisely.",
    "In Approaches, candidates often describe therapies without linking them to the underlying assumptions of the approach; explicit links earn AO2 credit.",
    "Timing is a common weakness: candidates should allocate roughly 30 minutes per section and leave time to check extended writing."
  ],
  "sourceRefs": ["S1", "grounded-web-research"]
}
